markdown_report:
At 20% progress, prioritize a small, baseline-preserving change: **residual depth aggregation inside NextItNet**, with prefix conditioning disabled initially.

Three starting insights motivate this choice. First, normalized depth aggregation previously scored 0.5175 versus the supplied cold start’s 0.5300. This supports testing a safer residual correction rather than assuming aggregation helps. Second, users report stale interests and broad relatedness displacing specific current matches. Positionwise depth selection could address both, although intermediate states do not guarantee forgetting. Third, Industrial_and_Scientific has an 8.22% sampled training wrong-ranking rate. This provides a measured discrimination target, while its effective rank of 8.12 alone does not establish a defect.

Three literature insights delimit the proposal. [NextItNet](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.05163) provides nested causal receptive fields. Selecting among them changes context emphasis without establishing intent boundaries. [Sampled-softmax research](https://wujcan.github.io/papers/tois-ssm.pdf) motivates stronger negative competition. Its collaborative-filtering findings do not establish transfer here. [Recformer](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.13731) motivates content sharing across items. Its pretrained representations do not validate text encoders trained from scratch.

These form three directions: context selection, ranking supervision, and content sharing. The framework is:

| Direction | Existing mechanism | Minimal experiment | Remaining gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| Context | NextItNet dilation | Residual depth correction | Actual suppression of stale information |
| Supervision | Sampled softmax | Multiple uniform negatives | False negatives and benchmark transfer |
| Content | Recformer text | Jointly trained title pooling | Sparse supervision without pretraining |

Three atomic ideas follow. Scores are originality/future potential/user alignment/model alignment/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Each cell gives a positive and a limitation.

| Idea | Originality | Potential | User alignment | Model alignment | Difficulty |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Residual depth correction | 4: localized adaptation; established gating | 7: controlled context study; redundant depths | 8: targets stale and broad matches; intent unobserved | 6: targets wrong rankings; mechanism unverified | 3: small head; masking care |
| Multi-negative softmax | 3: simple transfer; established objective | 7: stronger competition; false negatives | 5: sharper distinctions; weak recency mechanism | 8: direct discrimination objective; training-only evidence | 4: shared scorer; added compute |
| Title residual embedding | 4: constrained content sharing; established fusion | 6: sparse-item transfer; weak lexical supervision | 7: specific names; compatibility unresolved | 5: shared item evidence; no diagnosed lexical deficit | 6: small encoder; vocabulary and serialization |

Select residual depth correction for feasibility and continuity. Preserve the final-block path and add a zero-initialized scalar times gated, normalized depth differences. This explicitly targets stale-interest emphasis and broad matches outranking current-specific choices, plus sampled training misranking. These are hypotheses, not demonstrated improvements.

Compare baseline, static depth weights, and positionwise weights with unchanged training controls. Select exclusively by four-category macro validation HR@10; retain baseline on ties. Inspect prefix interventions only as supporting diagnostics. Deploy one jointly trained checkpoint per category, with identical training and predictor implementations.

idea.description: Add a baseline-preserving residual depth correction to the supplied corrected NextItNet. At each valid position, normalize existing residual-block states over channels, compute depth weights, and aggregate their differences from the normalized final state. Add that correction to the unmodified final-block state through one zero-initialized trainable scalar. Keep one item-scoring head and one independently trained checkpoint per category. Disable masked-prefix conditioning in the initial experiment.
idea.motivation: The selected idea explicitly targets two observed user-facing failures: older seasonal or secondary interests receiving excessive emphasis, and broadly related recommendations displacing specific matches to current purpose. Selecting among existing causal depths may change that emphasis, but cannot guarantee intent recognition or removal of old information. It also targets the measured model-facing sampled training misranking rate, especially Industrial_and_Scientific's 8.22% and Electronics' 6.67%. These measurements are descriptive training statistics, not validation HR@10. The earlier aggregation result of 0.5175 versus 0.5300 motivates preserving an exact final-state path instead of replacing it.
idea.implementation_notes:
Integrate the module below immediately after collecting existing block outputs and before the baseline's unchanged final feature transformation. The supplied baseline source is absent from the prompt, so this is an integration component rather than a fabricated replacement train.py. Every state must have shape B x L x D. Instantiate the module once in the model constructor, after baseline parameters are initialized and before creating the optimizer. Pass the identical class and configuration into the embedded predictor writer; strict-load its state_dict together with the backbone. Set mode='adaptive' for the proposal or mode='static' for the controlled comparison. The baseline control omits this module. No additional backbone passes or independent predictors are introduced.

The correction is h_final + alpha * sum_k weight_k * (LN(h_k) - LN(h_final)), with a shared, affine-free channel LayerNorm. Initialize alpha and all gate parameters to zero. For finite activations this initially preserves the final-block state exactly; gate gradients initially vanish while alpha can learn. Alpha is an unconstrained scalar, so weights alone do not measure effective use. The gate reads only same-position causal block states. There is no prefix average, timestamp feature, auxiliary scorer, or separately fitted component. All depths still execute, and their receptive fields overlap; shallow states can already include older information.

Keep the host baseline's loss, optimizer, sampler, embedding dimension, dilation schedule, and final transformation unchanged for this architectural comparison. Preserve left-only padding and mask inside existing blocks after biased convolutions, normalizations and residual updates. Mask aggregation outputs and exclude invalid targets from loss. Gather the largest nonzero sequence index at inference, handling empty histories with the supplied baseline convention. Preserve item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), view.model and every ModelView interface. The original structural diagnostic must recognize the added positionwise operations or report its reachability analysis as unavailable; it must not silently certify an outdated graph. Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions, and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Define any added gate statistics and distinguish them from ranking evidence.

Retain Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl routing; DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; preprocessing seed 0; training seed 42; maximum 200 epochs and exactly 200 batches per executed epoch. Run on one GPU and save all artifacts beneath the trial directory. Before execution, fix checkpoint inspection, stopping and tie-breaking rules and allocate the remaining shared 43,200 GPU-second budget across baseline, static and adaptive configurations, including failures and diagnostics. Each configuration trains from scratch without reading another trial's checkpoints. If three configurations cannot fit, drop the static control before examining scores and limit mechanistic claims. Select the configuration solely by pinned four-category macro validation HR@10, preferring baseline on exact ties. Do not change the evaluator or infer omitted diagnostic values. Use observed histories, titles, descriptions and timestamps only; ratings, reviews, prices, stores, item categories and simulator traits remain unavailable. Freeze one selected checkpoint per category and its matching predictor before held-out evaluation.
idea.pseudocode:
import torch
from torch import nn
import torch.nn.functional as F


class ResidualDepthCorrection(nn.Module):
    """One jointly trained feature layer within the existing NextItNet."""
    def __init__(self, num_blocks, hidden_dim, mode='adaptive'):
        super().__init__()
        if num_blocks < 1 or mode not in ('adaptive', 'static'):
            raise ValueError('Invalid depth correction configuration')
        self.num_blocks = num_blocks
        self.hidden_dim = hidden_dim
        self.mode = mode
        self.gate_weight = nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(num_blocks, hidden_dim))
        self.gate_bias = nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(num_blocks))
        self.alpha = nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(()))

    def forward(self, states, sequence):
        # states: existing causal block outputs, each B x L x D.
        if len(states) != self.num_blocks:
            raise ValueError('Checkpoint depth and backbone depth disagree')
        mask = sequence.ne(0).unsqueeze(-1)
        final = states[-1] * mask
        normalized = torch.stack([
            F.layer_norm(h, (self.hidden_dim,)) * mask
            for h in states
        ], dim=2)  # B x L x K x D
        if self.mode == 'adaptive':
            logits = torch.einsum(
                'blkd,kd->blk', normalized, self.gate_weight
            ) + self.gate_bias
        else:
            logits = self.gate_bias.view(1, 1, -1).expand(
                sequence.shape[0], sequence.shape[1], -1
            )
        weights = logits.softmax(dim=-1)
        delta = normalized - normalized[:, :, -1:, :]
        correction = (weights.unsqueeze(-1) * delta).sum(dim=2)
        return (final + self.alpha * correction) * mask

originality.positive: A specific baseline-preserving, difference-based aggregation of existing causal NextItNet depths provides a controlled extension of the starting idea.
originality.negative: Adaptive depth aggregation, feature gating and zero-initialized residual corrections are established techniques; substantial novelty is unproven.

future_potential.positive: Provides a low-cost foundation for controlled studies of depth selection, context emphasis and safe architectural initialization.
future_potential.negative: Existing states may be redundant, and depth selection may learn identity shortcuts without improving immediate-purpose relevance.

code_difficulty.positive: Adds a small feature module without changing the causal backbone, scoring interface, data requirements or number of deployed models.
code_difficulty.negative: Reliable integration still requires internal padding masks, diagnostic graph updates and identical checkpoint reconstruction in the predictor writer.

related_work.title: NextItNet: A Simple Convolutional Generative Network for Next Item Recommendation
contributions: Uses residual dilated causal convolutions to model sequential dependencies.
Supplies the required backbone and the intermediate states used by the proposed correction.
limitations: Expanded receptive fields do not establish intent boundaries or effective forgetting.
Does not validate the proposed adaptive residual depth correction.

related_work.title: On the Effectiveness of Sampled Softmax Loss for Item Recommendation
contributions: Analyzes sampled-softmax optimization and its emphasis on difficult negatives.
Motivates the alternative multi-negative supervision experiment.
limitations: Reported collaborative-filtering evidence does not establish improvement for this NextItNet benchmark.
Hard negative competition can emphasize false negatives and requires additional compute.

related_work.title: Recformer
contributions: Studies recommendation from item text and motivates sharing information across items through content.
Provides conceptual support for the alternative title-embedding direction.
limitations: Its pretrained language representations and Transformer architecture cannot be directly adopted under these constraints.
Its results do not establish that a randomly initialized title encoder improves this task.
